analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds three env-var rows at head lines 1756-1758 (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS). They are TTFT and memory tuning knobs in the daemon-drain passthrough list. The patch shows no change to the coordinator, attestation, App Attest, key custody or encrypted prefix-cache storage trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-011, T-041). It exposes no secret. The supplied inference.md units (head lines 1634-2439) sit outside the changed ranges (head 404-413 and 1095-1115), so they are unchanged context: Qwen3-VL reasoning seed, tool parser tables, MiMo and Flint notes, and no new control. The changed inference.md hunks were visible only as a truncated patch excerpt. They describe releasing retained free KV segments before eviction and a new design where released rows park free 64 MiB KV segments per pool (up to min(2 GiB, grant/8)), outside the grant and ledger charge, and reinstall them for the next same-size-class admission. The text cut off at 'New segments wrap zero-fil…'. The source implementation is not supplied. I cannot verify two points. First, whether reinstalled parked segments are zeroed or overwritten before reuse. Residual KV data across requests or tenants touches T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory) and A-001. Second, whether parked memory stays outside the ledger and could weaken memory-admission or DoS guarantees (T-029). The env knob SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS and SEGMENT_RETENTION suggest operator toggles that could disable zeroing or retention. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence, so no finding is raised. Integration should check the segment-retention code in EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift and GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift for cross-request data hygiene and accounting, and whether T-028 needs updating.
